dimensions.profile: Fast to act on operational fires, deliberately slow on structural changes. The migration recovery story shows 48-hour tactical response but a 90-day deliberate rebuild plan.

stories.prompt: Tell me about the last deadline that really mattered.
stories.narrative: The anchor customer gave us 30 days to show a plan. I had a war room running within two days, but I refused to promise fixes faster than we could actually deliver them, and told the customer exactly that.
signals: urgency on response, honesty on timelines
comfortable delivering unwelcome truth to a customer

dimensions.self_report: Describes self as 'impatient but not reckless'

dimensions.profile: Disagrees in private, commits in public. Pushed back on the CEO's plan to cut headcount mid-recovery; lost the argument, executed the cut, then documented the service impact and won the rehire case a quarter later.

stories.prompt: Last time you disagreed with your boss about something that mattered?
stories.narrative: I told the CEO cutting 15% of warehouse staff during the recovery would show up in error rates within six weeks. He did it anyway. I executed it cleanly, tracked the impact, and brought the data back. We rehired in Q3.

dimensions.profile: Does best work with quarterly goals and weekly written updates; chafes under daily check-ins. Best-manager story centers on being handed a failing site with full authority; worst-manager story is a daily-standup micromanager.

manager_manual.onboarding: Hand them the ugliest real problem on day one, not a listening tour. They build trust by fixing something visible fast.
manager_manual.feedback: Direct and private. They will argue back once; that's processing, not defiance. Decide, and they'll commit.
manager_manual.check_ins: Weekly written update plus a biweekly 1:1. Daily standups read as distrust.
manager_manual.motivators: Visible operational metrics improving; promoting their people.
manager_manual.demotivators: Being asked to promise timelines they don't believe; decisions relitigated after commitment.
manager_manual.communication: Writes first, talks second. Expect a memo before a meeting.
